title: Our Go-To Over-Ear Headphones Are at Their Lowest Price for Prime Day
gist: Nothing's Headphone (1) hits a record-low $189 ($110 off) for Prime Day; the reviewer credits its transparent design and physical controls, noting the design's success spawned a cheaper Headphone (a) and premium Headphone (1) Pro.

insights.claim: Nothing's Headphone (1), its first over-ear headphone launched in 2025, was successful enough that the brand followed with a lower-priced Headphone (a) and a premium Headphone (1) Pro.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Nothing is using design differentiation to build out a tiered audio line, a challenger brand gaining traction against incumbents.
insights.quote: The bold design was so successful that the brand followed up with the similar-looking but lower-priced

insights.claim: Headphone (1) differentiates with all-physical controls (wheel, rocker, switches) in a market dominated by touch controls, plus up to 35 hours of battery with ANC on.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Tactile UX is a viable differentiator in a commoditizing ANC category.
insights.quote: They are all physical, clicky wheels, rockers, and buttons, a far cry from most over-ear headphones on the market.
insights.locator: A big standout is the on-ear controls

insights.claim: The reviewer rates Nothing's ANC and sound as excellent but below $400-plus flagships from Sony, Bose and Apple, positioning it as the mid-tier value pick at $189 (37% off $299).
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Mid-tier challengers compete on price/design while incumbents hold the performance crown.
insights.quote: though not as top-tier as pricier, $400-plus headphones from Sony, Bose, and Apple
insights.locator: Noise cancellation, transparency, and sound quality
